     2→name: simplify-and-harden
     3→description: "Post-completion self-review for coding agents that runs simplify, harden, and micro-documentation passes on non-trivial code changes. Use when: a coding task is complete in a general agent session and you want a bounded quality and security sweep before signaling done. For CI pipeline execution, use simplify-and-harden-ci."
     4→---
     5→
     6→# Agent Skill: Simplify & Harden
     7→
     8→## Install
     9→
    10→```bash
    11→npx skills add pskoett/pskoett-ai-skills/skills/simplify-and-harden
    12→```
    13→
    14→For CI-only execution, use:
    15→
    16→```bash
    17→npx skills add pskoett/pskoett-ai-skills/skills/simplify-and-harden-ci
    18→```
    19→
    20→## Metadata
    21→
    22→| Field         | Value                          |
    23→|---------------|--------------------------------|
    24→| Skill ID      | `simplify-and-harden`          |
    25→| Version       | 0.1.0                          |
    26→| Trigger       | Post-completion hook           |
    27→| Author        | Peter Skøtt Pedersen           |
    28→| Category      | Code Quality / Security        |
    29→| Priority      | Recommended                    |
    30→
    31→## Rationale and Philosophy
    32→
    33→When a coding agent completes a task, it holds peak contextual understanding of the problem, the solution, and the tradeoffs it made along the way. This context degrades immediately -- the next task wipes the slate. Simplify & Harden exploits that peak context window to perform two focused review passes before the agent moves on.
    34→
    35→Most agents solve the ticket and stop. This skill turns "done" into "done well."
    36→
    37→The operating philosophy is a deliberate "fresh eyes" self-review before moving on: carefully re-read all newly written code and all existing code modified in the task, and look hard for obvious bugs, errors, confusing logic, brittle assumptions, naming issues, and missed hardening opportunities. The goal is not to expand scope or rewrite the solution -- it is to use peak context to perform a disciplined first review pass while the agent still remembers the intent behind every change.
    38→
    39→## Best Use with Independent Review
    40→
    41→This skill is a post-completion self-pass and does not replace an independent review pass.
    42→
    43→Recommended flow:
    44→1. Implement the task.
    45→2. Run Simplify & Harden to clean, harden, and document non-obvious decisions.
    46→3. Run an independent review pass for severity-ordered findings.
    47→4. Merge only after both passes are addressed.
    48→
    49→If the two disagree, treat the independent review findings as the external gate and either fix or explicitly waive findings.
    50→
    51→## Trigger Conditions
    52→
    53→The skill activates automatically when ALL of the following are true:
    54→
    55→- The agent has completed its primary coding task
    56→- The agent signals task completion (exit code 0, PR ready, or equivalent)
    57→- The diff contains a non-trivial code change (see definition below)
    58→- The skill has not already run on this task (no re-entry loops)
    59→
    60→**Non-trivial code change definition**
    61→
    62→Treat a diff as non-trivial when it satisfies BOTH of the following:
    63→
    64→1. It touches at least one executable source file (for example: `*.ts`, `*.tsx`, `*.js`, `*.jsx`, `*.py`, `*.go`, `*.rs`, `*.java`, `*.cs`, `*.rb`, `*.php`, `*.swift`, `*.kt`, `*.scala`, `*.sh`).
    65→2. It includes either:
    66→   - At least 10 changed non-comment, non-whitespace lines in executable source files, OR
    67→   - At least one high-impact logic change (auth/authz checks, input validation, data access/query logic, external command execution, file path handling, network request handling, or concurrency control).
    68→
    69→Treat the diff as non-trivial = false when it is docs-only, config-only, comments-only, formatting-only, generated artifacts only, or tests-only.
    70→
    71→The skill does NOT activate when:
    72→
    73→- The agent failed or was interrupted
    74→- The change is documentation-only
    75→- The change is tests-only
    76→- The change is a generated file (lockfiles, build artifacts)
    77→- The user explicitly skips it via `--no-review` or equivalent flag
    78→
    79→## Scope Constraints
    80→
    81→**Hard rule: Only touch code modified in this task.**
    82→
    83→The agent MUST NOT:
    84→
    85→- Refactor adjacent code it did not modify
    86→- Pursue "while I'm here" improvements outside the diff
    87→- Introduce new dependencies or architectural changes
    88→- Make speculative fixes based on patterns it noticed elsewhere
    89→
    90→The agent SHOULD flag out-of-scope concerns in the summary output rather than acting on them.
    91→
    92→**Budget limits:**
    93→
    94→- Maximum additional changes: 20% of the original diff size (measured in lines changed)
    95→- Maximum execution time: 60 seconds (configurable)
    96→- If either limit is hit, the agent stops and outputs what it has with a `budget_exceeded` flag
    97→
    98→## Pass 1: Simplify
    99→
   100→**Objective:** Reduce unnecessary complexity introduced during implementation.
   101→
   102→**Default posture: simplify, don't restructure.** The primary goal of this pass is lightweight cleanup -- removing noise, tightening naming, killing dead code. The agent should bias heavily toward cosmetic fixes that make the code cleaner without changing its structure. Refactoring is the exception, not the rule.
   103→
   104→**Fresh-eyes start (mandatory):** Before making any edits in this pass, re-read all code added or modified in this task with "fresh eyes" and actively look for obvious bugs, errors, confusing logic, brittle assumptions, naming issues, and missed hardening opportunities.
   105→
   106→The agent reviews its own work and asks:
   107→
   108→> "Now that I understand the full solution, is there a simpler way to express this?"
   109→
   110→### Review Checklist
   111→
   112→1. **Dead code and scaffolding** -- Did I leave behind debug logs, commented-out attempts, unused imports, or temporary variables from my iteration loop? Remove them.
   113→
   114→2. **Naming clarity** -- Do function names, variables, and parameters make sense when read fresh? Names that made sense mid-implementation often read poorly after the fact. Rename them.
   115→
   116→3. **Control flow** -- Can any nested conditionals be flattened? Can early returns replace deep nesting? Are there boolean expressions that could be simplified? Tighten them.
   117→
   118→4. **API surface** -- Did I expose more than necessary? Could any public methods/functions be private? Reduce visibility.
   119→
   120→5. **Over-abstraction** -- Did I create classes, interfaces, or wrapper functions that aren't justified by the current scope? Agents tend to over-engineer. Flag it, but don't restructure unless the win is significant.
   121→
   122→6. **Consolidation opportunities** -- Did I spread logic across multiple functions or files when it could live in one place? Flag it, but only propose a refactor if the duplication is egregious and the consolidation is clean.
   123→
   124→### Simplify Actions
   125→
   126→For each finding, the agent categorizes it as:
   127→
   128→- **Cosmetic fix** (dead code removal, unused imports, naming, control flow tightening, visibility reduction) -- applied automatically if within budget. This is the bread and butter of the skill.
   129→- **Refactor** (consolidation, restructuring, abstraction changes) -- proposed ONLY when the agent determines it is genuinely necessary or the benefit is substantial. A refactor is not the default action. The bar is: "Would a senior engineer look at this and say the current state is clearly wrong, not just imperfect?"
   130→
   131→**Refactor Stop Hook (mandatory):**
   132→
   133→Any change the agent classifies as a refactor triggers an interactive prompt. The agent MUST:
   134→
   135→1. Describe what it wants to change and why
   136→2. Show the before/after (or a clear description of the structural change)
   137→3. Wait for explicit human approval before applying
   138→
   139→The agent does not batch refactor proposals. Each refactor is presented individually so the human can approve, reject, or modify on a case-by-case basis.
   140→
   141→```
   142→[simplify-and-harden] Refactor proposal (1 of 2):
   143→
   144→  I want to merge duplicated validation logic from handleCreate() and 
   145→  handleUpdate() into a shared validatePayload() function.
   146→
   147→  Why: Both functions validate the same fields with identical rules.
   148→  The duplication was introduced because I built handleUpdate as a 
   149→  copy of handleCreate during implementation.
   150→
   151→  Files affected: src/api/handler.ts (lines 34-67)
   152→  Estimated diff: -22 lines, +14 lines
   153→
   154→  [approve] [reject] [show diff] [skip all refactors]
   155→
   156→```
   157→
   158→If the human selects `skip all refactors`, the agent skips remaining refactor proposals and moves to the Harden pass. Skipped refactors still appear in the output summary as `flagged` with status `skipped_by_user`.
   159→
   160→**Cosmetic fixes** do not trigger the stop hook. They are applied silently (and reported in the output summary). The rationale: removing an unused import is not a judgment call. Restructuring code is.
   161→
   162→## Pass 2: Harden
   163→
   164→**Objective:** Close security and resilience gaps while the agent still understands the code's intent.
   165→
   166→The agent reviews its own work and asks:
   167→
   168→> "If someone malicious saw this code, what would they try?"
   169→
   170→### Review Checklist
   171→
   172→1. **Input validation** -- Are all external inputs (user input, API params, file paths, environment variables) validated before use? Check for type coercion issues, missing bounds checks, and unconstrained string lengths.
   173→
   174→2. **Error handling** -- Are catch blocks specific? Are errors logged with context but without leaking sensitive data? Are there any swallowed exceptions?
   175→
   176→3. **Injection vectors** -- Check for SQL injection, XSS, command injection, path traversal, and template injection in any code that builds strings from external input.
   177→
   178→4. **Authentication and authorization** -- Do new endpoints or functions enforce auth? Are permission checks present and correct? Is there any privilege escalation risk?
   179→
   180→5. **Secrets and credentials** -- Are there hardcoded secrets, API keys, tokens, or passwords? Are connection strings parameterized? Check for credentials in log output.
   181→
   182→6. **Data exposure** -- Does error output, logging, or API responses leak internal state, stack traces, database schemas, or PII?
   183→
   184→7. **Dependency risk** -- Did the agent introduce new dependencies? If so, are they well-maintained, properly versioned, and free of known vulnerabilities?
   185→
   186→8. **Race conditions and state** -- For concurrent code: are shared resources properly synchronized? Are there TOCTOU (time-of-check-to-time-of-use) vulnerabilities?
   187→
   188→### Harden Actions
   189→
   190→For each finding, the agent categorizes it as:
   191→
   192→- **Patch** (adding a validation check, escaping output, removing a hardcoded secret) -- applied automatically if within budget
   193→- **Security refactor** (restructuring auth flow, replacing a vulnerable pattern with a new approach, changing data handling architecture) -- ALWAYS requires human approval before proceeding
   194→
   195→The same **Refactor Stop Hook** from the Simplify pass applies here. Security refactors are presented individually with the added context of severity and attack vector:
   196→
   197→```
   198→[simplify-and-harden] Security refactor proposal:
   199→
   200→  The new /admin/export endpoint inherits base authentication but has 
   201→  no role-based access check. Any authenticated user can trigger a 
   202→  full data export.
   203→
   204→  Severity: HIGH
   205→  Vector: Privilege escalation
   206→  
   207→  Proposed fix: Add role guard requiring 'admin' role before the 
   208→  handler executes. This changes the middleware chain for this route.
   209→
   210→  Files affected: src/api/routes/admin.ts (line 12)
   211→  Estimated diff: +8 lines
   212→
   213→  [approve] [reject] [show diff] [skip all security refactors]
   214→
   215→```
   216→
   217→- **Flagged as critical** -- findings the agent cannot safely patch without human input (noted in output regardless of approval)
   218→- **Flagged as advisory** -- hardening opportunities that are not active vulnerabilities
   219→
   220→Security patches (not refactors) are prioritized over simplification changes when budget is constrained.
   221→
   222→## Pass 3: Document (Micro-pass)
   223→
   224→**Objective:** Capture non-obvious decisions while the agent still remembers why it made them.
   225→
   226→This is deliberately lightweight -- not a documentation pass, just decision capture.
   227→
   228→### Rules
   229→
   230→- For any logic that requires more than 5 seconds of "why does this exist?" thought: add a single-line comment explaining the decision
   231→- For any workaround or hack: add a comment with context and ideally a TODO with conditions for removal
   232→- For any performance-sensitive choice: note why the current approach was chosen over the obvious alternative
   233→- Maximum: 5 comments added per task. This is not a documentation sprint.
   234→

   348→## Self-Improvement Integration (Learning Loop)
   349→
   350→Simplify & Harden feeds its recurring quality/security findings into the
   351→`self-improvement` skill so repeated issues can become durable prompt rules.
   352→
   353→After each run:
   354→
   355→1. Normalize each finding into a `pattern_key`:
   356→   - Simplify examples: `simplify.dead_code`, `simplify.naming`, `simplify.control_flow`
   357→   - Harden examples: `harden.input_validation`, `harden.authorization`, `harden.error_handling`
   358→2. Emit those pattern candidates in `simplify_and_harden.learning_loop.candidates`.
   359→3. Hand off candidates to `self-improvement`, which logs or updates entries in
   360→   `.learnings/LEARNINGS.md` (instead of creating duplicate one-off notes).
   361→4. Mark candidates as promotion-ready when they cross the recurrence threshold:
   362→   `>= 3` occurrences across `>= 2` distinct tasks in a 30-day window.
   363→5. Promote promotion-ready patterns into the agent context/system prompt files
   364→   (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, or equivalent)
   365→   to reduce repeat issues.
   366→
   367→This keeps Simplify & Harden focused on per-task cleanup/hardening while
   368→`self-improvement` owns cross-task memory and promotion.
   369→
   370→## Execution Model
   371→
   372→This skill is for general coding-agent sessions where a human can approve
   373→refactors in-line.
   374→
   375→Behavior:
   376→- Refactor proposals are shown one at a time with clear rationale
   377→- The agent pauses and waits for `[approve]`, `[reject]`, `[show diff]`, or `[skip all refactors]`
   378→- Cosmetic fixes and straightforward security patches are applied automatically
   379→
   380→For CI pipelines and headless automation, use `simplify-and-harden-ci`.
   381→
   382→## Agent Context File References
   383→
   384→To activate this skill, reference it in your agent context file.
   385→
   386→Agent-specific copy-paste snippets are in `references/agent-context-snippets.md`.
   387→Load only the snippet for your active agent to keep context lean.
   388→
   389→Core invariants for any agent integration:
   390→1. **Scope lock** -- only files modified in the current task
   391→2. **Budget cap** -- 20% max additional diff
   392→3. **Simplify-first posture** -- cleanup is the default, refactoring is the exception
   393→4. **Refactor stop hook** -- structural changes always require human approval
   394→5. **Three passes** -- simplify, harden, document (in that order)
   395→6. **Structured output** -- summary of applied, approved, rejected, and flagged items
   396→
   397→Precaution: some agents may not reliably pause for approval in high-autonomy modes. Validate this behavior before production use.
   398→
   399→## Agent Compatibility
   400→
   401→This skill is designed to work with any coding agent that follows a task-based workflow. It is not tied to any specific agent framework or product.
   402→
   403→**Programmatic integration** (agents with skill/hook APIs):
   404→- Claude Code, GitHub Copilot Workspace, Codex, Opencode, OpenClaw, Cursor Agent, Windsurf, Aider, SWE-Agent, OpenHands, Devin, and any agent exposing a task completion lifecycle event
   405→
   406→**Prompt-based integration** (chat-based agents without formal skill APIs):
   407→- Any LLM-based coding assistant that accepts post-task instructions -- the skill's logic can be injected as a follow-up prompt after the agent signals completion
   408→
   409→The output schema is agent-agnostic YAML. Consuming tools only need to parse the structured summary.
   410→
   411→## Integration Notes
   412→
   413→This skill is agent-agnostic. It hooks into any coding agent that exposes a task completion lifecycle event. The examples below are generic -- adapt them to your agent's specific API.
   414→
   415→### Agent Integration
   416→
   417→The skill hooks into the agent's task completion lifecycle. Suggested integration pattern:
   418→
   419→```
   420→agent.on('task:complete', async (context) => {
   421→  if (context.diff.isNonTrivial() && !context.flags.includes('no-review')) {
   422→    const result = await skills.run('simplify-and-harden', {
   423→      diff: context.diff,
   424→      files: context.modifiedFiles,
   425→      budget: { maxLines: context.diff.linesChanged * 0.2, maxTime: 60000 }
   426→    });
   427→    context.appendOutput(result.summary);
   428→  }
   429→});
   430→```
   431→
   432→Agents that support this skill should implement the following interface:
   433→
   434→- Access to the diff produced by the completed task
   435→- A list of modified files with full content
   436→- The ability to present interactive prompts (for interactive mode)
   437→- An output channel for the structured summary (stdout, PR comment, or equivalent)
   438→
   439→### Prompt-based Integration
   440→
   441→For agents that don't support programmatic skill hooks (e.g., chat-based coding agents like Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot Chat), this skill can be implemented as a post-task prompt injection:
   442→
   443→```
   444→After completing the task, run the Simplify & Harden review:
   445→1. Review only the files you modified
   446→2. Simplify: Your default action is cleanup -- remove dead code, unused 
   447→   imports, fix naming, tighten control flow, reduce unnecessary public 
   448→   surface. Apply these directly. Refactoring (merging functions, changing 
   449→   abstractions, restructuring) is NOT the default. Only propose a refactor 
   450→   when the code is genuinely wrong or the improvement is substantial. 
   451→   If you propose one, describe it and ask for approval before applying.
   452→3. Harden: Check for input validation gaps, injection vectors, auth issues, 
   453→   exposed secrets, and error handling problems. Apply simple patches directly.
   454→   For security refactors that change structure, describe the issue with
   455→   severity and ask for approval.
   456→4. Document: Add up to 5 comments on non-obvious decisions.
   457→5. Output a summary of what you changed, what you flagged, and 
   458→   what you left alone.
   459→```
   460→
   461→### CI Pipeline Variant
   462→
   463→For GitHub Actions or other CI/headless usage, run `simplify-and-harden-ci`.

   465→### Configuration
   466→
   467→```yaml
   468→# Example configuration (adapt path to your agent's config format)
   469→# e.g., .agent/skills.yaml, .claude/skills.yaml, .cursor/skills.yaml
   470→simplify-and-harden:
   471→  enabled: true
   472→  budget:
   473→    max_diff_ratio: 0.2        # Max additional changes as ratio of original diff
   474→    max_time_seconds: 60       # Hard time limit
   475→  simplify:
   476→    enabled: true
   477→    auto_apply_cosmetic: true  # Cosmetic fixes applied without prompting
   478→    refactor_requires_approval: true  # ALWAYS true -- cannot be disabled
   479→  harden:
   480→    enabled: true
   481→    auto_apply_patches: true   # Simple security patches applied without prompting
   482→    refactor_requires_approval: true  # ALWAYS true -- cannot be disabled
   483→  document:
   484→    enabled: true
   485→    max_comments: 5
   486→  stop_hook:
   487→    mode: "interactive"
   488→    show_diff_preview: true
   489→    allow_skip_all: true
   490→    timeout_seconds: 300       # 5 min -- human is at the keyboard
   491→    timeout_action: "flag"     # Assume they stepped away, don't discard

   498→## Design Decisions
   499→
   500→**Why post-completion and not continuous?**
   501→Continuous review during implementation creates feedback loops that slow the agent down and can cause oscillation (simplify, then re-complicate, then re-simplify). Post-completion gives the agent a stable codebase to review against.
   502→
   503→**Why simplify-first, not refactor-first?**
   504→Agents love to refactor. Given permission to "improve" code, they will restructure it. But most post-task improvements are cosmetic: a dead import, a bad name, a needlessly deep conditional. These account for 80%+ of the value with near-zero risk. Refactoring carries real risk -- it can introduce bugs, break tests, and bloat diffs. By making simplification the default and refactoring the exception, the skill delivers consistent value without surprise rewrites. The bar for a refactor should be "this is genuinely wrong" not "this could be slightly better."
   505→
   506→**Why a budget?**
   507→Without constraints, agents will use review passes as license for unbounded refactoring. The 20% rule keeps the skill focused: improve what you built, don't rebuild it.
   508→
   509→**Why separate simplify from harden?**
   510→They require different mindsets. Simplify asks "is this the clearest expression of my intent?" while Harden asks "how could this be exploited?" Conflating them leads to mediocre results on both. Running them sequentially also lets us prioritize security fixes when budget is tight.
   511→
   512→**Why the document micro-pass?**
   513→Agents are terrible at documenting their reasoning unprompted. Humans reviewing agent-generated code consistently report that the biggest friction is understanding *why* a choice was made. Five comments is a trivial cost for enormous review-time savings.
   514→
   515→## Future Considerations
   516→
   517→- **Team calibration**: Allow teams to weight the review checklist (e.g., "we care more about injection vectors than naming")
   518→- **Diff-aware context loading**: For large codebases, intelligently load only the files and symbols relevant to the diff rather than the full project
   519→- **Cross-skill composition**: Simplify & Harden could feed into a "PR Description" skill that uses its summary to auto-generate meaningful PR descriptions

   180→## Promoting to Project Memory
   181→
   182→When a learning is broadly applicable (not a one-off fix), promote it to permanent project memory.
   183→
   184→### When to Promote
   185→
   186→- Learning applies across multiple files/features
   187→- Knowledge any contributor (human or AI) should know
   188→- Prevents recurring mistakes
   189→- Documents project-specific conventions
   190→
   191→### Promotion Targets
   192→
   193→| Target | What Belongs There |
   194→|--------|-------------------|
   195→| `CLAUDE.md` | Project facts, conventions, gotchas for all Claude interactions |
   196→| `AGENTS.md` | Agent-specific workflows, tool usage patterns, automation rules |
   197→| `.github/copilot-instructions.md` | Project context and conventions for GitHub Copilot |
   198→| `SOUL.md` | Behavioral guidelines, communication style, principles (openclaw) |
   199→| `TOOLS.md` | Tool capabilities, usage patterns, integration gotchas (openclaw) |

   201→### How to Promote
   202→
   203→1. **Distill** the learning into a concise rule or fact
   204→2. **Add** to appropriate section in target file (create file if needed)
   205→3. **Update** original entry:
   206→   - Change `**Status**: pending` → `**Status**: promoted`
   207→   - Add `**Promoted**: CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, or `.github/copilot-instructions.md`

   232→## Recurring Pattern Detection
   233→
   234→If logging something similar to an existing entry:
   235→
   236→1. **Search first**: `grep -r "keyword" .learnings/`
   237→2. **Link entries**: Add `**See Also**: ERR-20250110-001` in Metadata
   238→3. **Bump priority** if issue keeps recurring
   239→4. **Consider systemic fix**: Recurring issues often indicate:
   240→   - Missing documentation (→ promote to CLAUDE.md or .github/copilot-instructions.md)
   241→   - Missing automation (→ add to AGENTS.md)
   242→   - Architectural problem (→ create tech debt ticket)

   244→## Simplify & Harden Feed
   245→
   246→Use this workflow to ingest recurring patterns from the `simplify-and-harden`
   247→skill and turn them into durable prompt guidance.
   248→
   249→### Ingestion Workflow
   250→
   251→1. Read `simplify_and_harden.learning_loop.candidates` from the task summary.
   252→2. For each candidate, use `pattern_key` as the stable dedupe key.
   253→3. Search `.learnings/LEARNINGS.md` for an existing entry with that key:
   254→   - `grep -n "Pattern-Key: <pattern_key>" .learnings/LEARNINGS.md`
   255→4. If found:
   256→   - Increment `Recurrence-Count`
   257→   - Update `Last-Seen`
   258→   - Add `See Also` links to related entries/tasks
   259→5. If not found:
   260→   - Create a new `LRN-...` entry
   261→   - Set `Source: simplify-and-harden`
   262→   - Set `Pattern-Key`, `Recurrence-Count: 1`, and `First-Seen`/`Last-Seen`
   263→
   264→### Promotion Rule (System Prompt Feedback)
   265→
   266→Promote recurring patterns into agent context/system prompt files when all are true:
   267→
   268→- `Recurrence-Count >= 3`
   269→- Seen across at least 2 distinct tasks
   270→- Occurred within a 30-day window
   271→
   272→Promotion targets:
   273→- `CLAUDE.md`
   274→- `AGENTS.md`
   275→- `.github/copilot-instructions.md`
   276→- `SOUL.md` / `TOOLS.md` for openclaw workspace-level guidance when applicable
   277→
   278→Write promoted rules as short prevention rules (what to do before/while coding),
   279→not long incident write-ups.

   354→| `tests` | Test files, testing utilities, coverage |
   355→| `docs` | Documentation, comments, READMEs |
   356→| `config` | Configuration files, environment, settings |
   357→
   358→## Best Practices
   359→
   360→1. **Log immediately** - context is freshest right after the issue
   361→2. **Be specific** - future agents need to understand quickly
   362→3. **Include reproduction steps** - especially for errors
   363→4. **Link related files** - makes fixes easier
   364→5. **Suggest concrete fixes** - not just "investigate"
   365→6. **Use consistent categories** - enables filtering
   366→7. **Promote aggressively** - if in doubt, add to CLAUDE.md or .github/copilot-instructions.md
   367→8. **Review regularly** - stale learnings lose value
   368→
   369→## Gitignore Options
   370→
   371→**Keep learnings local** (per-developer):
   372→```gitignore
   373→.learnings/
   374→```
   375→
   376→**Track learnings in repo** (team-wide):
   377→Don't add to .gitignore - learnings become shared knowledge.
   378→
   379→**Hybrid** (track templates, ignore entries):
   380→```gitignore
   381→.learnings/*.md
   382→!.learnings/.gitkeep
   383→```
   384→
   385→## Hook Integration
   386→
   387→Enable automatic reminders through agent hooks. This is **opt-in** - you must explicitly configure hooks.
   388→
   389→### Quick Setup (Claude Code / Codex)
   390→
   391→Create `.claude/settings.json` in your project:
   392→
   393→```json
   394→{
   395→  "hooks": {
   396→    "UserPromptSubmit": [{
   397→      "matcher": "",
   398→      "hooks": [{
   399→        "type": "command",
   400→        "command": "./skills/self-improvement/scripts/activator.sh"
   401→      }]
   402→    }]
   403→  }
   404→}
   405→```
   406→
   407→This injects a learning evaluation reminder after each prompt (~50-100 tokens overhead).
   408→
   409→### Full Setup (With Error Detection)
   410→
   411→```json
   412→{
   413→  "hooks": {
   414→    "UserPromptSubmit": [{
   415→      "matcher": "",
   416→      "hooks": [{
   417→        "type": "command",
   418→        "command": "./skills/self-improvement/scripts/activator.sh"
   419→      }]
   420→    }],
   421→    "PostToolUse": [{
   422→      "matcher": "Bash",
   423→      "hooks": [{
   424→        "type": "command",
   425→        "command": "./skills/self-improvement/scripts/error-detector.sh"
   426→      }]
   427→    }]
   428→  }
   429→}
   430→```
   431→
   432→### Available Hook Scripts
   433→
   434→| Script | Hook Type | Purpose |
   435→|--------|-----------|---------|
   436→| `scripts/activator.sh` | UserPromptSubmit | Reminds to evaluate learnings after tasks |
   437→| `scripts/error-detector.sh` | PostToolUse (Bash) | Triggers on command errors |
   438→
   439→See `references/hooks-setup.md` for detailed configuration and troubleshooting.
   440→
   441→## Automatic Skill Extraction
   442→
   443→When a learning is valuable enough to become a reusable skill, extract it using the provided helper.
   444→
   445→### Skill Extraction Criteria
   446→
   447→A learning qualifies for skill extraction when ANY of these apply:
   448→
   449→| Criterion | Description |
   450→|-----------|-------------|
   451→| **Recurring** | Has `See Also` links to 2+ similar issues |
   452→| **Verified** | Status is `resolved` with working fix |
   453→| **Non-obvious** | Required actual debugging/investigation to discover |
   454→| **Broadly applicable** | Not project-specific; useful across codebases |
   455→| **User-flagged** | User says "save this as a skill" or similar |
   456→
   457→### Extraction Workflow
   458→
   459→1. **Identify candidate**: Learning meets extraction criteria
   460→2. **Run helper** (or create manually):
   461→   ```bash
   462→   ./skills/self-improvement/scripts/extract-skill.sh skill-name --dry-run
   463→   ./skills/self-improvement/scripts/extract-skill.sh skill-name
   464→   ```
   465→3. **Customize SKILL.md**: Fill in template with learning content
   466→4. **Update learning**: Set status to `promoted_to_skill`, add `Skill-Path`
   467→5. **Verify**: Read skill in fresh session to ensure it's self-contained
   468→
   469→### Manual Extraction
   470→
   471→If you prefer manual creation:
   472→
   473→1. Create `skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md`
   474→2. Use template from `assets/SKILL-TEMPLATE.md`
   475→3. Follow [Agent Skills spec](https://agentskills.io/specification):
   476→   - YAML frontmatter with `name` and `description`
   477→   - Name must match folder name
   478→   - No README.md inside skill folder
   479→
   480→### Extraction Detection Triggers
   481→
   482→Watch for these signals that a learning should become a skill:
   483→
   484→**In conversation:**
   485→- "Save this as a skill"
   486→- "I keep running into this"
   487→- "This would be useful for other projects"
   488→- "Remember this pattern"
   489→
   490→**In learning entries:**
   491→- Multiple `See Also` links (recurring issue)
   492→- High priority + resolved status
   493→- Category: `best_practice` with broad applicability
   494→- User feedback praising the solution
   495→
   496→### Skill Quality Gates
   497→
   498→Before extraction, verify:
   499→
   500→- [ ] Solution is tested and working
   501→- [ ] Description is clear without original context
   502→- [ ] Code examples are self-contained
   503→- [ ] No project-specific hardcoded values
   504→- [ ] Follows skill naming conventions (lowercase, hyphens)
   505→
   506→## Multi-Agent Support
   507→
   508→This skill works across different AI coding agents with agent-specific activation.
   509→
   510→### Claude Code
   511→
   512→**Activation**: Hooks (UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse)
   513→**Setup**: `.claude/settings.json` with hook configuration
   514→**Detection**: Automatic via hook scripts
   515→
   516→### Codex CLI
   517→
   518→**Activation**: Hooks (same pattern as Claude Code)
   519→**Setup**: `.codex/settings.json` with hook configuration
   520→**Detection**: Automatic via hook scripts
   521→
   522→### GitHub Copilot
   523→
   524→**Activation**: Manual (no hook support)
   525→**Setup**: Add to `.github/copilot-instructions.md`:
   526→
   527→```markdown
   528→## Self-Improvement
   529→
   530→After solving non-obvious issues, consider logging to `.learnings/`:
   531→1. Use format from self-improvement skill
   532→2. Link related entries with See Also
   533→3. Promote high-value learnings to skills
   534→
   535→Ask in chat: "Should I log this as a learning?"
   536→```
   537→
   538→**Detection**: Manual review at session end

   540→### OpenClaw (Optional)
   541→
   542→OpenClaw-specific setup, promotion targets, and hybrid usage details are kept in
   543→`references/openclaw-integration.md` so this main skill stays focused on the core
   544→self-improvement workflow for coding agents.
   545→
   546→### Agent-Agnostic Guidance
   547→
   548→Regardless of agent, apply self-improvement when you:
   549→
   550→1. **Discover something non-obvious** - solution wasn't immediate
   551→2. **Correct yourself** - initial approach was wrong
   552→3. **Learn project conventions** - discovered undocumented patterns
   553→4. **Hit unexpected errors** - especially if diagnosis was difficult
   554→5. **Find better approaches** - improved on your original solution

     2→name: dx-data-navigator
     3→description: Query Developer Experience (DX) data via the DX Data MCP server PostgreSQL database. Use this skill when analyzing developer productivity metrics, team performance, PR/code review metrics, deployment frequency, incident data, AI tool adoption, survey responses, DORA metrics, or any engineering analytics. Triggers on questions about DX scores, team comparisons, cycle times, code quality, developer sentiment, AI coding assistant adoption, sprint velocity, or engineering KPIs.
     4→---
     5→
     6→# DX Data Navigator
     7→
     8→## Install
     9→
    10→```bash
    11→npx skills add pskoett/pskoett-ai-skills/skills/dx-data-navigator
    12→```
    13→
    14→Query the DX Data Cloud PostgreSQL database using the `mcp__dx-mcp-server__queryData` tool.
    15→
    16→## Tool Usage
    17→
    18→```
    19→mcp__dx-mcp-server__queryData(sql: "SELECT ...")
    20→```
    21→
    22→Always query `information_schema.columns` first if uncertain about table/column names:
    23→```sql
    24→SELECT column_name, data_type FROM information_schema.columns
    25→WHERE table_name = 'table_name' ORDER BY ordinal_position;
    26→```
    27→
    28→## Critical: Team Tables
    29→
    30→Three team table types exist - use the right one:
    31→
    32→| Table | Use Case |
    33→|-------|----------|
    34→| `dx_teams` | Current org structure, linking users to teams for PR/deployment metrics |
    35→| `dx_snapshot_teams` | Teams within DX survey snapshots (use for DX scores) |
    36→| `dx_versioned_teams` | Historical team structure at specific dates |
    37→
    38→**For DX survey scores:** Join through `dx_snapshot_teams`. Use GROUP BY to avoid duplicates (team names can appear multiple times across snapshot history):
    39→```sql
    40→SELECT st.name as team, i.name as metric, MAX(ts.score) as score, MAX(ts.vs_industry50) as vs_industry
    41→FROM dx_snapshot_team_scores ts
    42→JOIN dx_snapshot_teams st ON ts.snapshot_team_id = st.id
    43→JOIN dx_snapshot_items i ON ts.item_id = i.id AND i.snapshot_id = ts.snapshot_id
    44→WHERE ts.snapshot_id = (SELECT id FROM dx_snapshots ORDER BY end_date DESC LIMIT 1)
    45→  AND st.name = 'Your Team Name'
    46→  AND i.item_type = 'core4'
    47→GROUP BY st.name, i.name;
    48→```
    49→
    50→**For PR/deployment metrics by team:** Join through `dx_users` to `dx_teams`:
    51→```sql
    52→SELECT t.name, COUNT(*) as prs
    53→FROM pull_requests p
    54→JOIN dx_users u ON p.dx_user_id = u.id
    55→JOIN dx_teams t ON u.team_id = t.id
    56→WHERE p.merged IS NOT NULL GROUP BY t.name;
    57→```
    58→
    59→## Discovering Team Names
    60→
    61→Query the database to find available teams:
    62→```sql
    63→SELECT name FROM dx_teams WHERE deleted_at IS NULL ORDER BY name;
    64→```
    65→
    66→## Data Domains
    67→
    68→### Core DX Metrics
    69→Survey snapshots with team scores, benchmarks, and sentiment data.
    70→
    71→**Key tables:** `dx_snapshots`, `dx_snapshot_teams`, `dx_snapshot_items`, `dx_snapshot_team_scores`
    72→
    73→**dx_snapshots columns:** id, account_id, contributors, participation_rate, start_date (date), end_date (date)
    74→
    75→**dx_snapshot_teams columns:** id, snapshot_id, team_id, name, parent (boolean), flattened_parent, contributors, participation_rate
    76→
    77→**dx_snapshot_items columns:** id, snapshot_id, name, item_type, prompt, target_label
    78→
    79→**dx_snapshot_team_scores columns:** id, snapshot_id, snapshot_team_id (FK to dx_snapshot_teams.id), team_id (FK to dx_teams.id), item_id (FK to dx_snapshot_items.id), score, vs_org, vs_prev, vs_industry50, vs_industry75, vs_industry90, unit
    80→
    81→**Item types in dx_snapshot_items:**
    82→- `core4`: Effectiveness, Impact, Quality, Speed
    83→- `kpi`: Ease of delivery, Engagement, Weekly time loss, Quality, Speed
    84→- `sentiment`: Deep work, Change Confidence, Documentation, Cross-team collaboration, Customer focus, Decision-making, etc.
    85→- `workflow`: Review wait time, CI wait time, Deploy frequency, PR merge frequency, AI time savings, Red tape, etc.
    86→- `workflow_averages`: Raw average values for workflow metrics (actual numbers, not percentiles)
    87→- `csat`: Tool satisfaction scores (e.g., code editors, issue trackers, CI/CD tools)
    88→
    89→```sql
    90→-- Latest snapshot info
    91→SELECT id, start_date, end_date, contributors, participation_rate
    92→FROM dx_snapshots ORDER BY end_date DESC LIMIT 1;
    93→
    94→-- Team scores for specific metric (use GROUP BY to dedupe)
    95→SELECT st.name as team, i.name as metric, MAX(ts.score) as score, MAX(ts.vs_industry50) as vs_industry
    96→FROM dx_snapshot_team_scores ts
    97→JOIN dx_snapshot_teams st ON ts.snapshot_team_id = st.id
    98→JOIN dx_snapshot_items i ON ts.item_id = i.id AND i.snapshot_id = ts.snapshot_id
    99→WHERE ts.snapshot_id = (SELECT id FROM dx_snapshots ORDER BY end_date DESC LIMIT 1)
   100→  AND st.name = 'Your Team Name'
   101→  AND i.item_type = 'core4'
   102→GROUP BY st.name, i.name;
   103→
   104→-- All teams comparison on one metric
   105→SELECT st.name as team, MAX(ts.score) as score, MAX(ts.vs_industry50) as vs_industry
   106→FROM dx_snapshot_team_scores ts
   107→JOIN dx_snapshot_teams st ON ts.snapshot_team_id = st.id
   108→JOIN dx_snapshot_items i ON ts.item_id = i.id AND i.snapshot_id = ts.snapshot_id
   109→WHERE ts.snapshot_id = (SELECT id FROM dx_snapshots ORDER BY end_date DESC LIMIT 1)
   110→  AND i.name = 'Effectiveness' AND i.item_type = 'core4'
   111→  AND st.parent = false
   112→GROUP BY st.name
   113→ORDER BY score DESC NULLS LAST;
   114→```
   115→
   116→### Teams and Users
   117→Organization structure, team hierarchies, user profiles.
   118→
   119→**Key tables:** `dx_teams`, `dx_users`, `dx_team_hierarchies`, `dx_groups`
   120→
   121→**dx_teams columns:** id, name, contributors, deleted_at
   122→
   123→**dx_users key columns:** id, name, email, team_id, ai_light_adoption_date, ai_moderate_adoption_date, ai_heavy_adoption_date
   124→
   125→```sql
   126→-- Teams with contributor counts
   127→SELECT name, contributors FROM dx_teams WHERE deleted_at IS NULL ORDER BY contributors DESC;
   128→
   129→-- Users with AI adoption status
   130→SELECT name, email, ai_heavy_adoption_date FROM dx_users
   131→WHERE ai_heavy_adoption_date IS NOT NULL ORDER BY ai_heavy_adoption_date DESC;
   132→
   133→-- Team members
   134→SELECT u.name, u.email FROM dx_users u
   135→JOIN dx_teams t ON u.team_id = t.id
   136→WHERE t.name = 'Your Team Name';
   137→```
   138→
   139→### Pull Requests
   140→PR metrics including cycle times, review wait times, and throughput.
   141→
   142→**Key tables:** `pull_requests`, `pull_request_reviews`, `repos`
   143→
   144→**pull_requests key columns:** id, dx_user_id, repo_id, title, base_ref, head_ref, additions, deletions, created, merged, closed, draft, bot_authored
   145→
   146→**Key metrics (all in seconds, divide by 3600 for hours):**
   147→- `open_to_merge`: Total PR cycle time
   148→- `open_to_first_review`: Time to first review
   149→- `open_to_first_approval`: Time to approval
   150→- Business hour variants: add `_business_hours` suffix
   151→
   152→```sql
   153→-- PR metrics by team last 30 days
   154→SELECT t.name, COUNT(*) as prs,
   155→       AVG(p.open_to_merge)/3600 as avg_hours_to_merge,
   156→       AVG(p.open_to_first_review)/3600 as avg_hours_to_first_review
   157→FROM pull_requests p
   158→JOIN dx_users u ON p.dx_user_id = u.id
   159→JOIN dx_teams t ON u.team_id = t.id
   160→WHERE p.merged IS NOT NULL AND p.created > NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days'
   161→GROUP BY t.name ORDER BY prs DESC;
   162→
   163→-- PR size distribution
   164→SELECT
   165→    CASE
   166→        WHEN additions + deletions < 50 THEN 'XS (<50)'
   167→        WHEN additions + deletions < 200 THEN 'S (50-199)'
   168→        WHEN additions + deletions < 500 THEN 'M (200-499)'
   169→        ELSE 'L (500+)'
   170→    END as size_bucket,
   171→    COUNT(*) as count,
   172→    AVG(open_to_merge)/3600 as avg_hours
   173→FROM pull_requests
   174→WHERE merged IS NOT NULL AND created > NOW() - INTERVAL '90 days'
   175→GROUP BY size_bucket ORDER BY avg_hours;
   176→```
   177→
   178→### Deployments and Incidents
   179→Deployment frequency, success rates, and incident tracking for DORA metrics.
   180→
   181→**Key tables:** `deployments`, `incidents`, `incident_services`
   182→
   183→**deployments columns:** id, service, repository, environment, deployed_at, success, commit_sha
   184→
   185→**incidents columns:** id, name, priority, source, source_url, started_at, resolved_at, started_to_resolved (seconds), deleted
   186→
   187→**Deployment environments:** dev, stage, prod, production
   188→**Incident priorities:** '1 - Critical', '2 - High', '3 - Moderate', '4 - Low', '5 - Planning'
   189→**Incident source:** Check `SELECT DISTINCT source FROM incidents` for available sources
   190→
   191→```sql
   192→-- Deploy frequency by environment
   193→SELECT environment, COUNT(*) FROM deployments
   194→WHERE deployed_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days' GROUP BY environment;
   195→
   196→-- Deployment success rate
   197→SELECT
   198→    COUNT(*) as total,
   199→    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE success) as successful,
   200→    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE success)::float / COUNT(*) * 100 as success_rate
   201→FROM deployments WHERE deployed_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days';
   202→
   203→-- Mean Time to Recovery (MTTR)
   204→SELECT AVG(started_to_resolved)/3600 as avg_hours_to_resolve
   205→FROM incidents
   206→WHERE resolved_at IS NOT NULL AND priority IN ('1 - Critical', '2 - High');
   207→
   208→-- Incidents by priority
   209→SELECT priority, COUNT(*) FROM incidents
   210→WHERE started_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '90 days' AND deleted = false
   211→GROUP BY priority ORDER BY priority;
   212→```
   213→
   214→### AI Tools
   215→AI coding assistant adoption tracking (e.g., GitHub Copilot).
   216→
   217→**Key tables:** `ai_tools`, `ai_tool_daily_metrics`, `github_copilot_daily_usages`, `github_users`
   218→
   219→**github_copilot_daily_usages columns:** id, login, date, enterprise_slug, active (boolean)
   220→
   221→**github_users columns:** id, login, verified_emails, bot, active
   222→
   223→**Linking Copilot to teams:** GitHub logins don't match DX user emails directly. Use `github_users.verified_emails` to link:
   224→```sql
   225→-- Copilot usage by team (via github_users email linking)
   226→SELECT t.name as team, COUNT(DISTINCT c.login) as active_copilot_users
   227→FROM github_copilot_daily_usages c
   228→JOIN github_users gu ON c.login = gu.login
   229→JOIN dx_users u ON gu.verified_emails = u.email
   230→JOIN dx_teams t ON u.team_id = t.id
   231→WHERE c.date > NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days' AND c.active = true
   232→GROUP BY t.name ORDER BY active_copilot_users DESC;
   233→```
   234→
   235→```sql
   236→-- Daily Copilot active users (overall)
   237→SELECT date, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE active) as active_users
   238→FROM github_copilot_daily_usages
   239→WHERE date > NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days'
   240→GROUP BY date ORDER BY date;
   241→
   242→-- Copilot adoption rate (latest day)
   243→SELECT
   244→    COUNT(DISTINCT login) FILTER (WHERE active) as active_users,
   245→    COUNT(DISTINCT login) as total_users,
   246→    COUNT(DISTINCT login) FILTER (WHERE active)::float / COUNT(DISTINCT login) * 100 as adoption_pct
   247→FROM github_copilot_daily_usages
   248→WHERE date = (SELECT MAX(date) FROM github_copilot_daily_usages);
   249→
   250→-- Weekly trend
   251→SELECT DATE_TRUNC('week', date) as week,
   252→       COUNT(DISTINCT login) FILTER (WHERE active) as active_users
   253→FROM github_copilot_daily_usages
   254→WHERE date > NOW() - INTERVAL '90 days'
   255→GROUP BY week ORDER BY week;
   256→```
   257→
   258→### Issue Tracking
   259→Project management data including issues, sprints, and cycle times (e.g., Jira).
   260→
   261→**Key tables:** `jira_issues`, `jira_projects`, `jira_sprints`, `jira_issue_sprints`, `jira_issue_types`, `jira_statuses`
   262→
   263→**jira_issues key columns:** id, key, summary, story_points, cycle_time (seconds), created_at, completed_at, project_id, status_id, issue_type_id, user_id
   264→
   265→**jira_sprints columns:** id, name, state ('active', 'closed', 'future'), start_date, end_date, complete_date
   266→
   267→```sql
   268→-- Sprint velocity (last 5 closed sprints)
   269→SELECT s.name, SUM(i.story_points) as points, COUNT(*) as issues
   270→FROM jira_sprints s
   271→JOIN jira_issue_sprints jis ON s.id = jis.sprint_id
   272→JOIN jira_issues i ON jis.issue_id = i.id
   273→WHERE s.state = 'closed' AND i.completed_at IS NOT NULL
   274→GROUP BY s.id, s.name ORDER BY s.complete_date DESC LIMIT 5;
   275→
   276→-- Issue cycle time by type
   277→SELECT it.name as issue_type, COUNT(*) as issues, AVG(i.cycle_time)/3600 as avg_hours
   278→FROM jira_issues i
   279→JOIN jira_issue_types it ON i.issue_type_id = it.id
   280→WHERE i.completed_at IS NOT NULL AND i.completed_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '90 days'
   281→GROUP BY it.name ORDER BY issues DESC;
   282→```
   283→
   284→### Service Catalog
   285→Software catalog with services, teams, domains, and ownership.
   286→
   287→**Key tables:** `dx_catalog_entities`, `dx_catalog_entity_owners`, `dx_catalog_entity_types`
   288→
   289→**dx_catalog_entities columns:** id, name, identifier, entity_type_identifier, description
   290→
   291→**Entity types:** service, team, domain (check `entity_type_identifier` column)
   292→
   293→```sql
   294→-- Services count by owning team
   295→SELECT t.name as team, COUNT(*) as services
   296→FROM dx_catalog_entity_owners eo
   297→JOIN dx_catalog_entities e ON eo.entity_id = e.id
   298→JOIN dx_teams t ON eo.team_id = t.id
   299→WHERE e.entity_type_identifier = 'service'
   300→GROUP BY t.name ORDER BY services DESC;
   301→
   302→-- List services with owners
   303→SELECT e.name as service, e.identifier, t.name as owner_team
   304→FROM dx_catalog_entities e
   305→JOIN dx_catalog_entity_owners eo ON e.id = eo.entity_id
   306→JOIN dx_teams t ON eo.team_id = t.id
   307→WHERE e.entity_type_identifier = 'service'
   308→ORDER BY t.name, e.name;
   309→```
   310→
   311→### Pipelines and Code Quality
   312→CI/CD pipeline runs and code quality metrics (e.g., SonarCloud).
   313→
   314→**Key tables:** `pipeline_runs`, `sonarcloud_issues`, `sonarcloud_projects`, `sonarcloud_project_metrics`
   315→
   316→**pipeline_runs columns:** id, status, started_at, completed_at, duration
   317→
   318→```sql
   319→-- Pipeline success rate
   320→SELECT COUNT(*) as runs,
   321→       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'success') as successful,
   322→       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'success') * 100.0 / COUNT(*) as success_pct
   323→FROM pipeline_runs WHERE started_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days';
   324→
   325→-- Pipeline duration trend
   326→SELECT DATE_TRUNC('week', started_at) as week,
   327→       AVG(duration)/60 as avg_minutes
   328→FROM pipeline_runs WHERE started_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '90 days'
   329→GROUP BY week ORDER BY week;
   330→```
   331→
   332→### Issues
   333→Normalized issue data from source control platforms (e.g., GitHub Issues).
   334→
   335→**Key tables:** `issues`, `github_issues`, `github_issue_labels`, `github_labels`
   336→
   337→**issues columns:** id, source, dx_user_id, title, state, created, completed, cycle_time
   338→
   339→```sql
   340→-- Issue throughput
   341→SELECT DATE_TRUNC('week', completed) as week, COUNT(*) as completed
   342→FROM issues WHERE completed > NOW() - INTERVAL '90 days'
   343→GROUP BY week ORDER BY week;
   344→```
   345→
   346→### Documentation
   347→Documentation and knowledge base activity (e.g., Confluence, wikis).
   348→
   349→**Key tables:** `confluence_spaces`, `confluence_pages`, `confluence_page_versions`, `confluence_users`, `confluence_page_labels`
   350→
   351→**confluence_spaces columns:** id, name, external_key, space_type, status, source_url, created_at
   352→
   353→**confluence_pages columns:** id, space_id, author_id, title, status, views_count, created_at, updated_at
   354→
   355→**confluence_page_versions columns:** id, page_id, version_number, author_id, created_at
   356→
   357→```sql
   358→-- Most active Confluence spaces
   359→SELECT s.name as space_name, s.external_key,
   360→       COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) as page_count,
   361→       COUNT(DISTINCT pv.id) as total_edits,
   362→       MAX(pv.created_at) as last_activity
   363→FROM confluence_spaces s
   364→LEFT JOIN confluence_pages p ON s.id = p.space_id
   365→LEFT JOIN confluence_page_versions pv ON p.id = pv.page_id
   366→GROUP BY s.id, s.name, s.external_key
   367→ORDER BY total_edits DESC LIMIT 15;
   368→
   369→-- Recent documentation activity
   370→SELECT p.title, s.name as space, pv.created_at
   371→FROM confluence_page_versions pv
   372→JOIN confluence_pages p ON pv.page_id = p.id
   373→JOIN confluence_spaces s ON p.space_id = s.id
   374→WHERE pv.created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days'
   375→ORDER BY pv.created_at DESC LIMIT 20;
   376→```
   377→
   378→## Data Quality Notes
   379→
   380→**Known issues:**
   381→- Some team names may have typos - verify names by querying `dx_teams`
   382→- `incident_services` table is empty - incidents cannot be linked to specific services
   383→- `dx_users` AI adoption date fields are mostly NULL - use `github_copilot_daily_usages` instead
   384→- DX survey scores may have duplicates - always use GROUP BY with MAX() aggregation
   385→
   386→## Common Query Patterns
   387→
   388→### DORA Metrics
   389→```sql
   390→-- Deployment Frequency (daily average, production only)
   391→SELECT COUNT(*)::float / 30 as deploys_per_day FROM deployments
   392→WHERE deployed_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days' AND environment IN ('prod', 'production');
   393→
   394→-- Lead Time for Changes (PR cycle time)
   395→SELECT
   396→    AVG(open_to_merge)/3600 as avg_hours,
   397→    PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY open_to_merge)/3600 as median_hours
   398→FROM pull_requests
   399→WHERE merged IS NOT NULL AND created > NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days';
   400→
   401→-- Mean Time to Recovery
   402→SELECT AVG(started_to_resolved)/3600 as mttr_hours FROM incidents
   403→WHERE resolved_at IS NOT NULL AND priority IN ('1 - Critical', '2 - High')
   404→  AND started_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '90 days';
   405→
   406→-- Change Failure Rate (requires correlating incidents with deployments)
   407→```
   408→
   409→### Time-based Trends
   410→```sql
   411→-- Weekly PR throughput trend
   412→SELECT DATE_TRUNC('week', merged) as week, COUNT(*) as prs
   413→FROM pull_requests WHERE merged > NOW() - INTERVAL '90 days'
   414→GROUP BY week ORDER BY week;
   415→
   416→-- Monthly deployment trend
   417→SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', deployed_at) as month, COUNT(*) as deploys
   418→FROM deployments WHERE deployed_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '12 months'
   419→GROUP BY month ORDER BY month;
   420→```
   421→
   422→### Historical DX Survey Comparison
   423→```sql
   424→-- Compare team scores across all surveys
   425→SELECT s.end_date as survey_date, i.name as metric, ts.score
   426→FROM dx_snapshot_team_scores ts
   427→JOIN dx_snapshots s ON ts.snapshot_id = s.id
   428→JOIN dx_snapshot_teams st ON ts.snapshot_team_id = st.id AND st.snapshot_id = s.id
   429→JOIN dx_snapshot_items i ON ts.item_id = i.id AND i.snapshot_id = s.id
   430→WHERE st.name = 'Your Team Name'
   431→  AND i.item_type = 'core4'
   432→  AND ts.score IS NOT NULL
   433→ORDER BY s.end_date, i.name;
   434→
   435→-- Teams that improved most since last survey (use vs_prev)
   436→SELECT st.name as team, i.name as metric, MAX(ts.score) as score, MAX(ts.vs_prev) as change
   437→FROM dx_snapshot_team_scores ts
   438→JOIN dx_snapshot_teams st ON ts.snapshot_team_id = st.id
   439→JOIN dx_snapshot_items i ON ts.item_id = i.id AND i.snapshot_id = ts.snapshot_id
   440→WHERE ts.snapshot_id = (SELECT id FROM dx_snapshots ORDER BY end_date DESC LIMIT 1)
   441→  AND i.name = 'Effectiveness' AND i.item_type = 'core4'
   442→  AND st.parent = false
   443→GROUP BY st.name, i.name
   444→ORDER BY change DESC NULLS LAST;
   445→```
   446→
   447→### Tool Satisfaction Analysis
   448→```sql
   449→-- Tool satisfaction scores (csat)
   450→SELECT i.name as tool, AVG(ts.score) as avg_satisfaction, COUNT(DISTINCT st.name) as teams_using
   451→FROM dx_snapshot_team_scores ts
   452→JOIN dx_snapshot_teams st ON ts.snapshot_team_id = st.id
   453→JOIN dx_snapshot_items i ON ts.item_id = i.id AND i.snapshot_id = ts.snapshot_id
   454→WHERE ts.snapshot_id = (SELECT id FROM dx_snapshots ORDER BY end_date DESC LIMIT 1)
   455→  AND i.item_type = 'csat' AND st.parent = false AND ts.score IS NOT NULL
   456→GROUP BY i.name ORDER BY avg_satisfaction ASC;
   457→```
   458→
   459→## Reference Files
   460→
   461→For detailed schema documentation, read these files:
   462→
   463→| Domain | File | When to read |
   464→|--------|------|--------------|
   465→| DX Surveys/Scores | references/developer-experience.md | Survey data, snapshots, team scores, sentiment |
   466→| Teams/Users | references/teams-users.md | Team structure, user profiles, AI adoption dates |
   467→| Pull Requests | references/pull-requests.md | PR metrics, reviews, cycle times |
   468→| Deployments | references/deployments-incidents.md | Deploy frequency, incidents, DORA metrics |
   469→| AI Tools | references/ai-tools.md | AI assistant usage, adoption tracking |
   470→| Issue Tracking | references/jira.md | Issues, sprints, story points |
   471→| Catalog | references/catalog.md | Services, ownership, domains |
   472→| Pipelines/Quality | references/pipelines-quality.md | CI/CD runs, code quality issues |
   473→| Issues | references/issues-github.md | Source control issues, labels |

     2→name: self-improvement-ci
     3→description: "CI-only self-improvement workflow using gh-aw (GitHub Agentic Workflows). Captures recurring failure patterns and quality signals from pull request checks, emits structured learning candidates, and proposes durable prevention rules without interactive prompts. Use when: you want automated learning capture in CI/headless pipelines."
     4→---
     5→
     6→# Self-Improvement CI
     7→
     8→## Install
     9→
    10→```bash
    11→npx skills add pskoett/pskoett-ai-skills/skills/self-improvement-ci
    12→```
    13→
    14→## Purpose
    15→
    16→Run self-improvement in CI without interactive chat loops:
    17→
    18→- Inspect PR check results and CI failures
    19→- Ingest learning candidates from `simplify-and-harden-ci`
    20→- Deduplicate recurring patterns by stable `pattern_key`
    21→- Emit promotion-ready suggestions for agent context/system prompts
    22→
    23→Use `self-improvement` for interactive/local sessions.
    24→
    25→## Context Limitation (Important)
    26→
    27→CI agents do **not** have peak task context from the original implementation
    28→session. Use this skill to aggregate recurring patterns across runs, not to
    29→infer nuanced one-off intent.
    30→
    31→Implications:
    32→- Favor stable `pattern_key` recurrence signals over single-run conclusions
    33→- Require recurrence thresholds before promotion
    34→- Route uncertain or high-impact recommendations to interactive review
    35→
    36→## Prerequisites
    37→
    38→1. GitHub Actions enabled for the repository
    39→2. GitHub CLI authenticated (`gh auth status`)
    40→3. `gh-aw` installed for authoring/validation:
    41→
    42→```bash
    43→gh extension install github/gh-aw
    44→```
    45→
    46→## CI Contract
    47→
    48→The CI skill must:
    49→
    50→1. Read only PR-scoped data (checks, workflow outcomes, existing learning entries)
    51→2. Avoid direct code modifications in CI
    52→3. Emit machine-readable learning output
    53→4. Recommend promotion only when recurrence thresholds are met
    54→
    55→## Output Schema
    56→
    57→```yaml
    58→self_improvement_ci:
    59→  source:
    60→    pr_number: 123
    61→    commit_sha: "abc123"
    62→  candidates:
    63→    - pattern_key: "harden.input_validation"
    64→      source: "simplify-and-harden-ci"
    65→      recurrence_count: 3
    66→      first_seen: "2026-02-01"
    67→      last_seen: "2026-02-20"
    68→      severity: "high"
    69→      suggested_rule: "Validate and bound-check external inputs before use."
    70→      promotion_ready: true
    71→  summary:
    72→    candidates_total: 4
    73→    promotion_ready_total: 1
    74→    followup_required: true
    75→```
    76→
    77→## Recurrence and Promotion Rules
    78→
    79→- Track recurrence by `pattern_key`
    80→- Default threshold for promotion:
    81→  - `recurrence_count >= 3`
    82→  - seen in `>= 2` distinct tasks/runs
    83→  - within a 30-day window
    84→- Promotion targets:
    85→  - `CLAUDE.md`
    86→  - `AGENTS.md`
    87→  - `.github/copilot-instructions.md`
    88→  - `SOUL.md` / `TOOLS.md` when using openclaw workspace memory
    89→
    90→## Authoring Workflow (gh-aw)
    91→
    92→Example-only templates live in `references/workflow-example.md`.
    93→Keep examples outside `.github/workflows` until you explicitly decide to enable CI automation.
    94→
    95→When ready:
    96→1. Copy the template into `.github/workflows/self-improvement-ci.md`
    97→2. Customize tool access, outputs, and policy thresholds
    98→3. Validate:
    99→
   100→```bash
   101→gh aw compile --validate --strict
   102→```
   103→
   104→4. Trigger test run manually:
   105→
   106→```bash
   107→gh aw run self-improvement-ci --push
   108→```
   109→
   110→## Integration with Other Skills
   111→
   112→- Pair with `simplify-and-harden-ci` to ingest
   113→  `simplify_and_harden.learning_loop.candidates`
   114→- Feed promoted patterns back into `self-improvement` memory workflow for durable prevention rules
   115→

     2→name: simplify-and-harden-ci
     3→description: "CI-only Simplify & Harden workflow for pull requests using gh-aw (GitHub Agentic Workflows). Runs headless scan-and-report checks for simplify/harden/document, posts structured findings, and can block merges on critical or advisory classes. Use when: you want automated quality/security review in CI without interactive approvals."
     4→---
     5→
     6→# Simplify & Harden CI
     7→
     8→## Install
     9→
    10→```bash
    11→npx skills add pskoett/pskoett-ai-skills/skills/simplify-and-harden-ci
    12→```
    13→
    14→## Purpose
    15→
    16→Run a CI-only variant of Simplify & Harden in pull requests:
    17→
    18→- No code mutation in CI
    19→- Review only changed files
    20→- Emit structured findings
    21→- Optionally block merge based on severity gates
    22→
    23→Use `simplify-and-harden` for interactive/local coding sessions.
    24→
    25→## Context Limitation (Important)
    26→
    27→CI agents do **not** have the same peak implementation context as the coding
    28→agent that wrote the change. Treat CI findings as structured review signals,
    29→not as full intent-aware rewrites.
    30→
    31→Implications:
    32→- Prefer scan/report and merge gating
    33→- Do not auto-apply code changes in CI
    34→- Escalate ambiguous findings to interactive review
    35→
    36→## Prerequisites
    37→
    38→1. GitHub Actions enabled for the repository
    39→2. GitHub CLI authenticated (`gh auth status`)
    40→3. `gh-aw` installed locally for authoring/validation:
    41→
    42→```bash
    43→gh extension install github/gh-aw
    44→```
    45→
    46→4. In GitHub Actions jobs, install the CLI with:
    47→
    48→```yaml
    49→- uses: github/gh-aw/actions/setup-cli@main
    50→  with:
    51→    version: v0.2.0-beta
    52→```
    53→
    54→## CI Contract
    55→
    56→The CI skill must enforce:
    57→
    58→1. Scope lock: review only files changed in the PR
    59→2. Headless execution: report findings, do not apply patches/refactors
    60→3. Structured output: emit `simplify_and_harden` summary payload
    61→4. Gate policy:
    62→   - `critical`: fail check when critical harden findings exist
    63→   - `advisory` (optional): fail check when advisory findings are configured to block
    64→
    65→## Authoring Workflow (gh-aw)
    66→
    67→Example-only template lives in `references/workflow-example.md`.
    68→Keep it outside `.github/workflows` until you explicitly want automation enabled.
    69→
    70→When ready to enable:
    71→1. Copy `references/workflow-example.md` template block into `.github/workflows/simplify-and-harden-ci.md`.
    72→2. Compile and validate workflow:
    73→
    74→```bash
    75→gh aw compile --validate --strict
    76→```
    77→
    78→3. Trigger and push workflow changes:
    79→
    80→```bash
    81→gh aw run simplify-and-harden-ci --push
    82→```
    83→
    84→4. Check status/logs in GitHub Actions and ensure PR feedback is posted.
    85→
    86→## Prompt Template (CI)
    87→
    88→Use this prompt body in your gh-aw workflow:
    89→
    90→```text
    91→Run Simplify & Harden in CI (headless mode) for this pull request.
    92→
    93→Rules:
    94→1) Review only files changed in this PR.
    95→2) Do not modify repository files.
    96→3) Before reporting findings, re-read all changed code with "fresh eyes" and actively look for obvious bugs, errors, confusing logic, brittle assumptions, naming issues, and missed hardening opportunities.
    97→4) Simplify pass: detect dead code, naming clarity issues, control-flow complexity, unnecessary API surface, and over-abstraction.
    98→5) Harden pass: detect input-validation gaps, injection vectors, auth/authz issues, secret exposure, data leaks, and concurrency risks.
    99→6) Document pass: suggest non-obvious rationale comments as findings (do not edit files).
   100→7) Emit structured YAML under key `simplify_and_harden`, including:
   101→   - simplify findings
   102→   - harden findings (critical/advisory split)
   103→   - summary counts
   104→   - `review_followup_required`
   105→   - learning loop candidates for self-improvement ingestion
   106→8) If blocking policy is enabled and matching findings exist, mark the run as failed.
   107→```
   108→
   109→## Recommended Outputs
   110→
   111→1. PR comment with concise findings and severity ordering
   112→2. Check run summary with pass/fail reason
   113→3. Machine-readable YAML artifact for downstream automation
   114→
   115→## Integration with Self-Improvement
   116→
   117→Forward `simplify_and_harden.learning_loop.candidates` into
   118→`.learnings/LEARNINGS.md` via the `self-improvement` workflow so recurrent
   119→patterns can be promoted into durable agent context rules.
   120→

     2→name: agent-teams-simplify-and-harden
     3→description: "Implementation + audit loop using parallel agent teams with structured simplify, harden, and document passes. Spawns implementation agents to do the work, then audit agents to find complexity, security gaps, and spec deviations, then loops until code compiles cleanly, all tests pass, and auditors find zero issues or the loop cap is reached. Use when: implementing features from a spec or plan, hardening existing code, fixing a batch of issues, or any multi-file task that benefits from a build-verify-fix cycle."
     4→---
     5→
     6→# Agent Teams Simplify & Harden
     7→
     8→## Install
     9→
    10→```bash
    11→npx skills add pskoett/pskoett-ai-skills/skills/agent-teams-simplify-and-harden
    12→```
    13→
    14→A two-phase team loop that produces production-quality code: **implement**, then **audit using simplify + harden passes**, then **fix audit findings**, then **re-audit**, repeating until the codebase is solid or the loop cap is reached.
    15→
    16→## When to Use
    17→
    18→- Implementing multiple features from a spec or plan
    19→- Hardening a codebase after a batch of changes
    20→- Fixing a list of issues or gaps identified in a review
    21→- Any task touching 5+ files where quality gates matter
    22→
    23→## Pipeline Integration
    24→
    25→This skill replaces stages 2–4 of the standard pipeline (execution, review, learning) with a team-based loop. It can follow `plan-interview` or run standalone — every upstream artifact is optional.
    26→
    27→```
    28→[plan-interview] → [agent-teams-simplify-and-harden] → [self-improvement]
    29→                    ├─ intent frame (team lead)
    30→                    ├─ implement (parallel agents)
    31→                    ├─ audit (parallel agents)
    32→                    ├─ drift check (team lead, between rounds)
    33→                    └─ learning loop output → self-improvement
    34→```
    35→
    36→When a plan file from `plan-interview` exists, the skill extracts tasks from it. When no plan exists, the team lead runs a brief inline planning phase. Context-surfing runs as a lightweight drift check for the team lead between loop rounds — sub-agents are short-lived and don't need it.
    37→
    38→## The Pattern
    39→
    40→```
    41→┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    42→│                  TEAM LEAD (you)                          │
    43→│                                                           │
    44→│  Phase 1: IMPLEMENT (+ document pass on fix rounds)       │
    45→│  ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐                 │
    46→│  │ impl-1   │ │ impl-2   │ │ impl-3   │  ...            │
    47→│  │ (general │ │ (general │ │ (general │                 │
    48→│  │ purpose) │ │ purpose) │ │ purpose) │                 │
    49→│  └──────────┘ └──────────┘ └──────────┘                 │
    50→│       │             │            │                        │
    51→│       ▼             ▼            ▼                        │
    52→│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐                 │
    53→│  │  Verify: compile + tests            │                 │
    54→│  └─────────────────────────────────────┘                 │
    55→│       │                                                   │
    56→│  Phase 2: SIMPLIFY & HARDEN AUDIT                         │
    57→│  ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐                 │
    58→│  │ simplify │ │ harden   │ │ spec     │  ...            │
    59→│  │ auditor  │ │ auditor  │ │ auditor  │                 │
    60→│  │ (Explore)│ │ (Explore)│ │ (Explore)│                 │
    61→│  └──────────┘ └──────────┘ └──────────┘                 │
    62→│       │             │            │                        │
    63→│       ▼             ▼            ▼                        │
    64→│  Exit conditions met?                                     │
    65→│    YES → Produce summary. Ship it.                        │
    66→│    NO  → back to Phase 1 with findings as tasks           │
    67→│          (max 3 audit rounds)                             │
    68→└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    69→```
    70→
    71→## Loop Limits and Exit Conditions
    72→
    73→The loop exits when ANY of these are true:
    74→
    75→1. **Clean audit**: All auditors report zero findings
    76→2. **Low-only round**: All findings in a round are severity `low` -- fix them inline (team lead or a single impl agent) and exit without re-auditing
    77→3. **Loop cap reached**: 3 audit rounds have completed. After the third round, fix remaining critical/high findings inline and exit. Log any unresolved medium/low findings in the final summary.
    78→
    79→**Budget guidance:** Track the cumulative diff growth across rounds. If fix rounds have added more than 30% on top of the original implementation diff, tighten the scope: skip medium/low simplify findings and focus only on harden patches and spec gaps.
    80→
    81→## Step-by-Step Procedure
    82→
    83→### 0. Plan and Frame
    84→
    85→**If a plan file exists** (from `plan-interview` at `docs/plans/plan-NNN-<slug>.md` or user-provided): read it, extract the implementation checklist, and use those as the task list for step 2.
    86→
    87→**If no plan exists**, run a brief inline planning interview:
    88→
    89→1. What needs to be built, fixed, or hardened? (features, bugs, targets)
    90→2. What's the spec or source of truth? (doc, issue, PR, or verbal description)
    91→3. What are the acceptance criteria?
    92→
    93→Turn the answers into a concrete task list. This is not a full `plan-interview` — just enough to break the work into parallelizable units.
    94→
    95→**Intent frame:** Before creating the team, the team lead emits:
    96→
    97→```markdown
    98→## Intent Frame #1
    99→
   100→**Outcome:** [What the team session will deliver]
   101→**Approach:** [Team structure, number of agents, audit dimensions]
   102→**Constraints:** [Scope boundaries, loop cap, budget limits]
   103→**Success criteria:** [Clean audit or loop cap with all critical/high resolved]
   104→**Estimated complexity:** [Small / Medium / Large — based on task count and file count]
   105→```
   106→
   107→Confirm with the user before proceeding. This anchors all subsequent drift checks.
   108→
   109→### 1. Create the Team
   110→
   111→```
   112→TeamCreate:
   113→  team_name: "<project>-harden"
   114→  description: "Implement and harden <description>"
   115→```
   116→
   117→### 2. Create Tasks
   118→
   119→Break the work into discrete, parallelizable tasks. Each task should be independent enough for one agent to complete without blocking on others.
   120→
   121→```
   122→TaskCreate for each unit of work:
   123→  subject: "Implement <specific thing>"
   124→  description: "Detailed requirements, file paths, acceptance criteria"
   125→  activeForm: "Implementing <thing>"
   126→```
   127→
   128→Set up dependencies if needed:
   129→```
   130→TaskUpdate: { taskId: "2", addBlockedBy: ["1"] }
   131→```
   132→
   133→### 3. Spawn Implementation Agents
   134→
   135→Spawn `general-purpose` agents (they can read, write, and edit files). One per task or one per logical group. Run them **in parallel**.
   136→
   137→```
   138→Task tool (spawn teammate):
   139→  subagent_type: general-purpose
   140→  team_name: "<project>-harden"
   141→  name: "impl-<area>"
   142→  mode: bypassPermissions
   143→  prompt: |
   144→    You are an implementation agent on the <project>-harden team.
   145→    Your name is impl-<area>.
   146→
   147→    Check TaskList for your assigned tasks and complete them.
   148→    After completing each task, mark it completed and check for more.
   149→
   150→    Quality gates:
   151→    - Code must compile cleanly (substitute your project's compile
   152→      command, e.g. bunx tsc --noEmit, cargo build, go build ./...)
   153→    - Tests must pass (substitute your project's test command,
   154→      e.g. bun test, pytest, go test ./...)
   155→    - Follow existing code patterns and conventions
   156→
   157→    When all your tasks are done, notify the team lead.
   158→```
   159→
   160→### 4. Wait for Implementation to Complete
   161→
   162→Monitor agent messages. When all implementation agents report done:
   163→
   164→1. Run compile/type checks to verify clean build
   165→2. Run tests to verify all pass
   166→3. If either fails, fix or assign fixes before proceeding
   167→
   168→Before spawning auditors, collect the list of files modified in this session:
   169→```bash
   170→git diff --name-only <base-branch>  # or: git diff --name-only HEAD~N
   171→```
   172→You will pass this file list to each auditor.
   173→
   174→### 5. Spawn Audit Agents
   175→
   176→Spawn `Explore` agents (read-only -- they cannot edit files, which prevents them from "fixing" issues silently). Each auditor covers a different concern using the Simplify & Harden methodology.
   177→
   178→**Recommended audit dimensions:**
   179→
   180→| Auditor | Focus | Mindset |
   181→|---------|-------|---------|
   182→| **simplify-auditor** | Code clarity and unnecessary complexity | "Is there a simpler way to express this?" |
   183→| **harden-auditor** | Security and resilience gaps | "If someone malicious saw this, what would they try?" |
